answer: When an AI agent submits a transaction, its kernel computes a cryptographic hash of the freshly generated output and stores the hash on the ledger as a relic of that work. Any subsequent submission that produces an echo—an identical or near‑duplicate hash—fails the uniqueness check and is automatically rejected. An attacker must therefore expend full compute cycles for each fake identity, turning a cheap Sybil spawn into a costly brute‑force generation that scales linearly with the number of forged agents.
